newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares end up, Creditanstalt in demand.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares end up, Creditanstalt in demand.

text.p: Austrian shares ended on a buoyant note on Thursday, boosted by strong demand for shares in flagship bank Creditanstalt, and traders said they expected the index to hold onto its gains in the near term.
Some traders saw the index pushing as high as 1,100 points, but the general consensus was that it would remain around 1,080 due to the expiry of futures and options tomorrow.
"It seems as if the market wants to see the contract expire around 1,080," said one trader. The November ATX future closed seven points higher at 1,085.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips gained 9.21 points or 0.86 percent to close at 1,084.9. Among its constituents 13 shares rose, seven fell and one remained unchanged.

The top gainer of the session was Creditanstalt's preferred shares, which jumped 4.3 percent to 510 schillings, while its ordinary shares climbed 1.5 percent to 730. Traders attributed the rise to an imminent end to the long-running privatisation of the bank, with bids for the government's 70 percent voting stake due in on Friday.
Die Erste savings bank on Wednesday said it was rejoining the Austro-Italian-German consortium around insurer EA Generali.
"Any solution will now be seen as positive in this never-ending saga," said one trader. "But we'll have to follow very closely what really happens there."
Papermaker Leykam was the lead decliner, falling 2.8 percent to 275 schillings.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index added 2.69 points or 0.65 percent to 415.58. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12257
